results.question: Can I take a ferry to La Gomera from the south of the island?

results.answer: Yes, you can take a ferry to La Gomera from the south of Tenerife. Los Cristianos Port has daily ferry connections to La Gomera, operated by Fred Olsen and Armas ferry companies (Source 4). Several day trip tours also depart from South Tenerife with hotel pickup included, making it convenient to reach the port (Sources 1, 3).

results.question: How do I get from the airport to the south of the island?
retrieved: San Cristóbal de La Laguna – By plane
Airport Transfer to Playa de las Américas
Puerto de la Cruz – By plane

results.answer:
You have several options to reach the south of the island from the airport (Sources 1, 3, 5):

• **By bus**: Titsa buses run from both airports to other towns, though you may need to change routes. They operate from around 05:00-06:00 until midnight.

• **By taxi**: From Tenerife South Airport (the closer option), it's only about 15 minutes to Los Cristianos in the south. From the northern airport, taxis are also available but the journey is longer.

• **By private transfer**: You can pre-book a private airport transfer with fixed fares and meet-and-greet service (Source 4).

• **By car**: If renting a car, take the TF-1 motorway from either airport to reach the southern areas (Source 3).

results.question: Where can I take the kids to swim near Los Cristianos?
results.answer: Los Cristianos has great options for swimming with kids! You can visit the **Piscina municipal (public swimming pool)** in town, or take advantage of the area's famous **sandy beaches** that Los Cristianos is known for (Source 1, 6). If your kids enjoy more adventure, there's also the **Xplore Tenerife Kayaking tour** which is beginner-friendly and includes snorkelling—it requires a minimum age of 14 and the ability to swim (Source 4).

results.question: What is there to see in La Laguna?
retrieved: San Cristóbal de La Laguna – Introduction

results.answer: La Laguna's historic centre is a UNESCO World Heritage Site well worth exploring on its own (Source 1). Key sights include churches along Calle de San Agustín – the Church of the Immaculate Conception, Casa Salazar, Church of St. Dominic, and Church-convent of Santa Catalina de Siena – accessible with a single €2 ticket (Source 2). The most important religious building is the Royal Sanctuary of the Christ of La Laguna on Plaza San Francisco, which houses the venerated Cristo de La Laguna and an exact replica of the Shroud of Turin (Source 3). You can also visit the Leal Theater, an impressively renovated eclectic-style theatre, or the Anaga National Park Visitor Centre to pick up hiking maps (Source 4).

results.question: Is it cold at the top of the volcano?
retrieved: San Cristóbal de La Laguna – Climate
Secret Volcano Tuk Tuk Tour: Tenerife & Adeje
results.answer: Yes, it's very cold at the top of El Teide. Even if beaches are warm, the summit can be freezing with snow common until March/April. Strong winds at the peak significantly reduce the apparent temperature even further. You'll also need strong sun protection since the rocks offer little shelter from the elements. (Source 3)

results.question: What local food should I try in Tenerife?
retrieved: Tenerife – Other water activities and tours
results.answer:
You should definitely try traditional Canarian dishes at **guachinches** – local taverns serving homemade food like grilled fish, roasted meat, and various stews, all for just a few euros. These places also serve their own wine, giving you an authentic local experience (Source 1).

For drinks, sample **local wines** from the north of the island, particularly those made from the malvasia grape variety with a long export tradition, or try **Dorada** and **Reine** beers produced locally. The island also produces unique **banana liqueurs** thanks to its abundant fruits (Source 4).

If you want fresh fish, head to Santa Cruz de Tenerife or ask locals for recommendations – plenty of good fish is available, though a dictionary might help with the names (Source 3).

results.question: ¿Cómo puedo llegar al Teide?
results.answer: Puedes llegar al Teide Nacional Park en alrededor de 90 minutos desde La Orotava o Vilaflor (Fuente 5). Una vez allí, tienes varias opciones: subir en el **teleférico del Teide** (Teleférico del Teide Base Station a 2,356m) para alcanzar los 3,555m en 8 minutos, o hacer **senderismo** si prefieres una experiencia más activa. También puedes explorar el parque en **buggy** con tours guiados que suben hasta 2,200m (Fuente 2, 4).
